discovery: Topological and geometric phases in quantum mechanics (Aharonov-Bohm effect and Berry phase)

nominees.name: Yakir Aharonov
nominees.affiliation: Tel Aviv University and Chapman University

motivation: Aharonov (with the late David Bohm) showed that electromagnetic potentials, not just fields, have physical effects on quantum particles: a charge picks up a measurable phase when it circles a flux it never touches. Berry showed that any quantum system carried slowly around a closed loop in parameter space acquires a geometric phase that depends only on the path. Together these results made gauge potentials and wavefunction geometry into observable physics. They were confirmed decisively in electron holography, interferometry and cold-atom experiments. Geometric and topological phases now sit at the base of the quantum Hall effect, topological insulators, band topology, synthetic gauge fields for ultracold atoms, and proposals for fault-tolerant quantum computing. Both men started from what many people then treated as a 'forbidden' question about the meaning of quantum theory, and the answers changed how the whole field thinks about it. This recognition is long overdue.
